_doc.purpose: Single source of truth for which skills are physically copied into a generated project. create-project copies from it; validate-project computes the same expected set and fails on a missing required skill or an unexpected extra one.
_doc.not_this: It does not control when a skill body loads into context. Physical inheritance keeps the capability available; agents still load skill content on demand rather than walking every skill.
_doc.inherited_set: generated project skills = INHERITED-STANDARD + the fixed Next profile's profile_skills. Nothing else. This file classifies a skill; the fixed Next profile decides which profile-inherited skills it takes -- one owner per decision.

distribution.builder-only: Stays in the Builder. Never copied.
distribution.inherited-standard: Copied into every generated project, regardless of profile.
distribution.profile-inherited: Copied when the fixed Next profile lists it in profile_skills.
distribution.optional: NOT copied. Stays in the Builder and reaches a project only through an explicit later decision. Copying it by default would make 'requires explicit human approval' a sentence in a document rather than a property of the repository.

_doc.ceiling: Project skills are dropped silently past roughly 28. A generated project receives the 17 standard skills plus the fixed Next profile's 2 additions -- 19 total. Adding to the standard set is not free.

artifact-design.purpose: Materialize an approved visual direction as a real, inspectable page.

atomic-design.purpose: Component identity, reuse-first, variants, duplication vs over-abstraction. Conceptual only -- it does not impose atoms/molecules/organisms directories.

frontend-design.purpose: Design methodology: typography, colour, spacing, layout, motion, and the judgement about what reads as generic.

ui-ux-pro-max.purpose: Design intelligence corpus with a CLI front door -- palettes, font pairings, styles, UX guidelines.

humanizalo.purpose: Product prose that reads as written by a person. Subordinate to specs, brand voice, technical and legal accuracy, and approved SEO.

deep-research.purpose: Multi-angle research when a single search would give a shallow or one-sided answer.

web-reader.purpose: Read a reference URL into concrete values -- palette, type, layout rhythm, component patterns. Used at Discovery, and again whenever the human points at a site during later changes.

building-components.purpose: Composition, accessibility patterns, prop shape and token systems for shared components.

emil-design-eng.purpose: Micro-interaction and motion craft -- what makes an interface feel considered rather than decorated.

navigation-shell.purpose: Headers, sticky behaviour, mobile menus and dashboard sidebars, and the accessibility criteria they fail by default.

redesign-existing-projects.purpose: Structured audit and targeted upgrade of something that already exists, instead of rewriting blindly.

web-design-guidelines.purpose: Review a built interface against web interface guidelines.

playwright-cli.purpose: Interactive browser inspection, evidence and debugging. Distinct from Playwright Test, which stays primary for reproducible E2E.

performance-audit.purpose: Grep-verified performance findings with file:line citations, as a Quality Gate input.

seo-audit.purpose: SEO checks, applied according to the product intent recorded in design.md -- a private app legitimately gets minimal metadata.

accessibility-audit.purpose: axe plus keyboard, focus, forms, dialogs, dynamic state and reflow. An axe pass is not an accessibility pass.

vercel-deploy.purpose: Deploy through the Vercel MCP. No silent CLI fallback for remote operations.

shadcn-ui.purpose: Component library patterns for React + Tailwind.

vercel-react-best-practices.purpose: React and Next performance rules, as progressive disclosure -- the index loads, a rule loads when relevant.

chrome-bridge-automation.purpose: Vision-driven automation through the human's own Chrome. Exceptional path only -- Playwright is first choice.
chrome-bridge-automation.not_inherited: Deliberately absent from every generated project. It drives the human's real browser with their live sessions and cookies, so it reaches a project only when someone decides it should, never because it came in the box.
